cards.explanation: The answer is that God will strike them out of his hands. God tells Ezekiel, His prophet, what will happen to Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. He says, “Then I will strike the bow from your left hand and dash down the arrows from your right hand.” Gog shows up armed, and his weapons get knocked right out of his hands.

The answer is False. God doesn't single Gog out for falling while everybody else slips off. He says, “On the mountains of Israel you will fall…” and then names Gog's troops and the nations with him as falling too. That's the whole crowd, friends, not one guy taking the hit for everybody.

The answer is that God says it is because He has spoken. God says Gog will fall in the open field, “…for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.” He gives no list of reasons, friends. His word is the reason, and it's plenty.

The answer is that they will know He is the LORD. God says He will send fire on Magog and on those in the coastlands, “…and they will know that I am the LORD.” That's how the verse ends, friends. It says it plainly, with no fancy words.

The answer is that it will surely happen. God says, “Yes, it is coming, and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD.” Then He adds, “This is the day of which I have spoken.” He doesn't leave any maybe in it, friends.

The answer is that they will burn them as fuel. God says those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out, kindle fires and burn up the weapons. “For seven years they will use them for fuel.” Everything from the bucklers and shields to the clubs and spears goes into the fire, friends (Ezekiel 39:9).

The answer is True, and what a turnaround, friends. God says they “…will loot those who looted them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD.” I think whoever did the taking is in for a real surprise. And look how that verse comes in two matching halves, so it's hard to miss.

The answer is Hamon-gog. God says Gog and all his hordes will be buried in the Valley of the Travelers, “So it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.” The name comes straight from the burying, friends.

The answer is cleanse. God says, “For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land.” He uses the word again in verse 16: “…And so they will cleanse the land.” And at the end of the seven months, friends, they begin a search for the invaders who remain on the ground (Ezekiel 39:14).

The answer is False. God says the one who sees a human bone “…will set up a pillar next to it, until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.” So the passerby doesn't bury it on the spot, friends. The pillar marks the place, and the burying ends up with the gravediggers, in the valley.

The answer is True. God tells Ezekiel to call out to every kind of bird and every beast of the field: “Assemble and come together from all around to the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you, a great feast on the mountains of Israel.” The birds and beasts are the ones being called (Ezekiel 39:17). I think this is a heavy part, friends.

The answer is the judgment He executes. God says, “I will display My glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment that I execute and the hand that I lay upon them.” It's a serious line, friends, so I think it's worth reading slowly.

The answer is that they were unfaithful to God. God says the nations will know “…that the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they were unfaithful to Me.” That's the reason, friends, and He states it Himself. It's a hard line, and He doesn't dress it up.
The answer is True. God says, “…because they were unfaithful to Me. So I hid My face from them…” He tells it plainly, friends. It's a heavy part, and He doesn't pretend otherwise.

The answer is that God will restore them from captivity. After the "Therefore," God says, “Now I will restore Jacob from captivity and will have compassion on the whole house of Israel…” The story turns here, friends, from exile toward bringing them back. It's a good turn.

The answer is forget. God says, “They will forget their disgrace and all the treachery they committed against Me, when they dwell securely in their land, with no one to frighten them.” It comes when they dwell securely in their land, friends. I think it's a gentle promise.

The answer is holiness. God says, “When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, I will show My holiness in them in the sight of many nations.” Notice who does the showing, friends. It's God, and He does it in them. I think that means the nations won't be looking at Israel's résumé, they'll be looking at what God did.

The answer is False. God says He will regather them to their own land, “…not leaving any of them behind after their exile among the nations.” He means everybody, friends, and He doesn't miss a single one. It's the kind of gathering where no one gets left standing at the door.

The answer is Spirit. God says, “And I will no longer hide My face from them, for I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.” I think it's a good place to land, friends, because the passage ends with His face no longer hidden.
